It sounds like you're carrying a lot of worry for your child, and it's clear you want to protect them—your care really comes through here.

To answer directly: yes, there are many options beyond Zoloft. There are several different antidepressants, and people can respond very differently to each one—your bad experience doesn't mean your child would have the same. Medication is also just one piece; therapy (like CBT or DBT) is often central for depression in young people, sometimes with or without medication. A child and adolescent psychiatrist can help weigh the options with you and your child.

Because your child is having suicidal thoughts, please treat this as urgent. If they're in immediate danger, call 911 or go to the nearest emergency room. You can also call or text 988 (Suicide & Crisis Lifeline) anytime for support and guidance—it's available for parents too. You don't have to figure this out alone.
